notes: כָּל־אִישׁ → *Whosoever he be* is retained whole: the subtraction test finds no English the ASV spends on one morpheme in particular, so rule 30's one-rendering condition holds and the formula's pronoun and copula belong to it, as rule 30 gives נָא's formula its pronouns. The competing reading marking *he be* `added` and heading on אִישׁ is named in the unit note.

Both object markers take the prepositions by which the English verbs reach their objects — *rebel against*, *hearken unto* — under rule 16's first family, while לְ before כֹל takes its own written *in* (rule 11); the ASV writes three words for three morphemes there, so no *whithersoever*-style fusion arises as it does at JOS.1.7, 1.9 and 1.16.
*he shall be put to death* is light verb plus complement headed on *death* (rule 44), with the subject pronoun and auxiliary kept with the verb under rule 17.
